sections.thesis: Treasuries rallied in a flight to quality as stocks sold off, taking the 10-year yield to its lowest level since Sept. 9.

sentences.text: Treasuries rallied in a flight to quality as stocks sold off, taking the 10-year yield to its lowest level since Sept. 9.
Two-year yields are down 17bp since before the election, and the odds of a December Fed hike fell to 65%.
Cleveland Fed President Hammack still said policy needs to move to a restrictive stance.

sections.thesis: The yen gained as Bank of Japan minutes read as a case for a December hike, helped by the fall in US tech stocks.

sentences.text: The yen gained as Bank of Japan minutes read as a case for a December hike, helped by the fall in US tech stocks.
USD/JPY dropped from just under 159.00 to just above 157.50.
The BoJ held at 1.25% on October 30 by eight votes to one and meets next on December 17-18.

sections.thesis: US stocks shed $3.2tn on fears that the Democrats' midterm sweep will cool the AI spending boom.

sentences.text: US stocks shed $3.2tn on fears that the Democrats' midterm sweep will cool the AI spending boom.
The Nasdaq 100 plunged 6.4% and Nvidia 9.3%, while the S&P 500 lost 4.4%, its worst session since last year's "Liberation Day" selloff.
Asia followed on Friday: South Korea's KOSPI fell more than 8%, triggering a circuit breaker, and Japan's Nikkei slumped 6%.

sections.thesis: Oil rebounded on Thursday as traders reconsidered whether the midterm results would bring a swift end to the Iran war.

sentences.text: Oil rebounded on Thursday as traders reconsidered whether the midterm results would bring a swift end to the Iran war.
Brent climbed to $98.01 by early afternoon, after plunging 8.7% on Wednesday to settle at $94.62.
Saudi Aramco cut its Arab Light price for Asian buyers by $2/bbl as Gulf producers compete for share with Hormuz flows recovering.
Gold climbed some 1% to trade above $4,100.
